f4b4bb981e:163b065d3b29a229.title: Vexto - Incident Response Desktop App UI UX
f4b4bb981e:163b065d3b29a229.summary: Vexto is a desktop app that gives our dispatch team real-time visibility into every vehicle in the fleet. It brings live GPS tracking, accident detection, and webcam verification into one system, so we can confirm incidents faster, respond with full context, and keep the whole operation under control. The project moved from fleet data audit to system architecture, incident logic, and map-based UX flows. Time was spent aligning live GPS, accident detection, and webcam feeds into one platform. The deepest work was structuring real-time logic that stays reliable at scale. We prioritized map-first navigation over list-based menus, since dispatchers think in location, not records. Analysis showed incident context mattered more than raw data, so we surfaced vehicle status, connectivity, and live webcam access in one card ? cutting verification time and improving response control.

f4b4bb981e:45ba4d56110252b6.title: Global Digital Collaboration Conference
f4b4bb981e:45ba4d56110252b6.summary: Visual identity for the Global Digital Collaboration Conference 2026 in Geneva. GDC brings together governments, international organisations, technology companies and other stakeholders to collaborate on the digital infrastructure and standards that increasingly connect our world. At the heart of the identity is the Global Barcode, an idea conceived by GDC founder Daniel Goldscheider. It translates the flags of all UN member states into simple vertical colour codes, based on the colours and their proportions within each national flag. Put together, they form one global code. And one very, very long flag. This became the starting point for the visual identity: an endless flag that folds, bends and winds its way through posters, spaces, shirts, lanyards and the conference itself. For the participant badges, the principle became personal: each name generates its own individual colour code.

f4b4bb981e:eaf91ce84cda68fb.title: Bradesco - São João
f4b4bb981e:eaf91ce84cda68fb.summary: We were invited by Lovely to create this São João campaign for Bradesco, inspired by the friendly rivalry between Caruaru and Campina Grande, home to two of Brazil's biggest June festivals. Building on the campaign concept, we developed a visual language inspired by Northeastern Brazilian folk culture and the tradition of repente, a form of improvised poetic dueling built around rhymes, wit, and playful provocation. We created a series of handcrafted illustrations that bring these two cities together, exploring the colors, shapes, and visual elements associated with São João celebrations. Each composition was designed to capture the spirit of rivalry while also celebrating a sense of unity. The result is a series of pieces that turn rivalry into connection and visually express the campaign's central message: the greatest São João is the one we create together.

f4b4bb981e:ec58b8cd447803b8.title: FoundersCard
f4b4bb981e:ec58b8cd447803b8.summary: FoundersCard has built a unique proposition around access?connecting an ambitious community of entrepreneurs and business leaders with exceptional benefits, experiences, and opportunities. Our challenge was to create a digital experience that felt as considered and valuable as the membership itself. We began by rethinking the experience from the ground up. Stripping away complexity, sharpening the hierarchy, and creating a clearer way to communicate the breadth of the FoundersCard world. The goal was simple: make something premium without feeling exclusive for the sake of it, and sophisticated without becoming complicated. A new visual language brought that thinking to life. Bold typography, confident layouts, elevated imagery, and a more editorial approach gave the brand greater presence and personality. A flexible design system created consistency across the experience while leaving room for partners, benefits, destinations, and stories to each have their own moment.

f4b4bb981e:e51223be3b54545f.summary: Halloween Costumes is an illustration project created as part of Inktober 2025. f4b4bb981e:c0e7c3d31d22a25e.title: SCS Ingegneria - website illustration
f4b4bb981e:c0e7c3d31d22a25e.summary: SCS Ingegneria is an engineering company based in Italy and specializing in renewable energy, infrastructure, and industrial projects. For the redesign of their website, I was commissioned to create a complete set of custom illustrations for every page. The goal wasn't to explain the technical side of their work, but to tell the story behind it. From the start, the client wanted the illustrations to capture the positive impact their projects have on people, the environment, and the places where they are built. Instead of treating renewable energy infrastructure as something that disrupts the landscape, the illustrations imagine it as part of it, living alongside nature and the communities around it.

f4b4bb981e:3875c0ab30f5f488.title: Tron: Ares ? Computer Vision
f4b4bb981e:3875c0ab30f5f488.summary: What does perception look like when it belongs to a machine? That question became the foundation for our work on TRON: Ares, where our team of twenty artists designed and animated more than sixty shots of computer vision and interface systems that visualize the world through the eyes of Ares. Rather than creating traditional HUD graphics, we set out to design machine perception itself. Every frame exists as a living system that continuously scans, tracks, evaluates, and reconstructs reality as streams of computation. Driven by a philosophy of maximum detail, each live action plate was transformed through our custom squarepacking algorithms into a computational lattice capable of analyzing the image at multiple scales simultaneously. Source code, reactive graphics, tracking systems, and layered analysis become different expressions of the same intelligence, revealing a world where every pixel is continuously interpreted and every image is rewritten through the language of the machine.

This collection brings them together as an ongoing exploration of character design, shape, personality and visual storytelling ? from friendly little monsters to weird creatures and mischievous ghosts. Created as a personal character design project, the collection explores playful horror, fantasy, humor and expressive silhouettes while keeping a strong focus on personality and storytelling. The collection is still growing, with new creatures joining the lineup from time to time. If you're looking for character design, creature design, illustration or visual development for a project, I'd love to hear from you.

a4977d3fa4:351b20d6bfce5055.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:351b20d6bfce5055.summary: SummaryDonatella Versace joins Revolve for a 2027 brand launch; Glenn Martens leaves Diesel following his SS27 show.Jacquemus opens a Miami flagship; Dior schedules its Cruise 2028 runway for Shanghai.Nike unveils its NYC design archive; Teyana Taylor stars in Calvin Klein’s Fall campaign.Glenn Marten's Diesel SS27 Collection Was a Party About PleasureGlenn Martens concluded his transformative six-year tenure at Diesel with a spectacular send-off for the Spring/Summer 2027 season. Announced just days before the event, his departure marked the end of an era that reinvigorated the Italian denim label. Martens ensured his final runway was a memorable celebration, opening the club-inspired venue with a sensual performance art piece by the Marseille collective (LA)HORDE. The hefty 90-look collection delivered the quintessential Diesel ethos: disruptive, fluid, and fun. Highlights included inventive hybrid garments like "pantasocks," trompe l’oeil outerwear, and denim laser-cut to mimic leather. Softening the industrial edge, recurring orchid-shaped cutaways added an organic touch to the distressed fabrics. Martens’s final bow leaves behind a lasting legacy of inclusivity and pop-cultural relevance.Dontella Versace Is Launching a New BrandFollowing her departure as Chief Creative Officer of Versace in 2025, Donatella Versace is preparing her next major industry move. The Italian designer is partnering with retail giant Revolve Group to launch a brand-new fashion and beauty label in 2027. The yet-to-be-named venture aims to combine Versace's creative authority with Revolve’s expansive technological infrastructure and global reach. Revolve, which reported $1.23 billion in revenue last year, offers a massive platform for the designer to build something from scratch. Versace noted that the collaboration is rooted in a shared belief that culture stems from connection, promising a fresh voice, look, and energy. a4977d3fa4:ce436292e82f8688.title: Off-White's "10x10: Icons Reimagined" Comes to Life at Milan's "Imaginary Palace"
a4977d3fa4:ce436292e82f8688.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:ce436292e82f8688.summary: Summary Off-White™'s "10x10: Icons Reimagined" project invited 10 global creatives to reinterpret 10 iconic Off-White pieces, culminating in the "IMAGINARY PALACE" exhibition during Milan Fashion Week.The exhibition ran from September 23–24 at Off-White's Milan space, showcasing final pieces alongside their creative references and process. Off-White™ unveiled its “10x10: Icons Reimagined” project with “IMAGINARY PALACE," a two-day exhibition during Milan Fashion Week, illuminating the exponential potential of creative collaboration. The “10x10: Icons Reimagined” project manifested earlier this year, inviting 10 global creative forces to approach 10 of its most recognizable icons as blank canvases — starting points for personal interpretation, experimentation, and rebellion. From musicians Scott Mescudi and A$AP Nast to designers Ava Nirui, Yuta Hosokawa, Raul Lopez, and Guillermo Andrade to multidisciplinary creatives Renell Medrano, Veneda Carter, Stéphane Ashpool, and Bafic, every 10x10 creator committed to following their personal vision, hacking the system, and taking their icon into the future by questioning everything. Spanning different disciplines, perspectives, and communities, the project replaced fixed rules with individual points of view. The resulting works are not homages, but continuations, opening the Off-White™ archive to transformation, allowing its legacy to evolve through the voices shaping culture and design today.Grammy Award-winning musician and fashion designer Scott Mescudi returns the "Out Of Office” sneaker to its sport codes while proposing the product as a platform — embracing use, movement, and freedom of expression. Photographer and director Renell Medrano applies her distinct perspective to new eyewear, turning her blank canvas into an investigation of looking, being seen, and perspective. Fashion designer and creative director Ava Nirui transforms the T-shirt, bringing her signature gender-neutral viewpoint and ’90s youth culture…

a4977d3fa4:e4f3c84cd8777133.title: Jil Sander's Next PUMA Pack Strips Back the Classics
a4977d3fa4:e4f3c84cd8777133.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:e4f3c84cd8777133.summary: SummaryJil Sander and PUMA are releasing minimalist, stripped-back versions of the classic Speedcat and Suede sneakers for SS27.The collaboration features monochromatic colorways and slim silhouettes, though an official release date and price remain unconfirmed.Jil Sander and PUMA are returning to refresh two PUMA classics through a lens of subtraction. ⁠Previewed at the Milan Fashion Week SS27 runway show by guests like King Princess and Space Afrika, the designer label is coming out with a stripped-back variant of the PUMA Speedcat and the PUMA Suede.⁠Instead of adding to the design of the Speedcat, creative director Simone Bellotti reduces it, replacing the signature Formstrip with a perforated shadow. ⁠Other than the small, golden Jil Sander logo on the lacing system, the Black colorway is entirely monochromatic, giving the smoothly shaped silhouette a luxurious feel in full leather. Taking after the Black colorway, the White Speedcat is also completely monochromatic; however, for those who prefer the signature detail, the white colorway boasts a streamlined suede Formstrip for variety. The new Jil Sander x Speedcat is also joined by a white Jil Sander x PUMA Suede, featuring tonal details to complete the lineup.⁠The partners' latest collaboration takes after the SS26 Jil Sander x PUMA K-Street, which dialled in on the slim-sneaker trend. "In recent years, the slim silhouette has become very fashionable again, but I’m not someone who really follows fashion; it’s something I have always liked," he said in an April interview with Hypebeast. "I’m not a huge fan of the big, chunky silhouettes. A very slim silhouette feels more “pure” in a way; it goes to the essence of the meaning of a shoe, without having too much design or material over it," he added.As of the time of writing, Jil Sander nor PUMA has confirmed the official release date or retail price. a4977d3fa4:adb814c584371a09.title: Toyota Prepares Us for Moon Festival With Its Curated Starter Packs
a4977d3fa4:adb814c584371a09.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:adb814c584371a09.summary: Mid-Autumn calls for good company under a full moon, so we've teamed up with Toyota to curate three ways to celebrate – each paired with the vehicle built to get you there. The idea is intentional rather than elaborate — good tea, a few sweets, and a lantern doing most of the work once everyone drifts toward the balcony. It’s a gathering built to fit however many square feet you’ve got, structured around ritual rather than production.What's inside:Set the table with a snow-skin mooncake keepsake box from Man Fu Yuan.A pot of osmanthus oolong by Harney & Sons, poured from the KINTO “Leaves to Tea” teapot and cup set.Keep the leaves fresh between pours with a Kaikado copper tea caddy.Candied osmanthus sweets and traditional mooncakes travel out to the balcony in a Hasami Porcelain stacking set.Once outside, a Noguchi Akari paper lantern takes over the lighting.Round out the atmosphere with APFR incense and a brass holder.When the moon climbs higher, break out a vintage mahjong set to keep hands busy while everyone watches the sky.Toyota C-HR – "The Performer" Moon Festival Starter PackThe Toyota C-HR’s sharp, city-quick handling makes it the natural fit for The Performer’s rooftop take on Mid-Autumn, where a moon-viewing turns a bare roof into a venue everyone’s actually excited to be at. This one runs loud and late, built less around a sit-down dinner and more around a rotating cast of drinks, music, and whoever shows up next. a4977d3fa4:12842c51534fdfe3.title: Nike Opens Its Massive Archive at New York’s Museum of Arts and Design
a4977d3fa4:12842c51534fdfe3.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:12842c51534fdfe3.summary: Summary “Nike: Form Follows Motion” traces the brand from early running experiments to Air, Flyknit and Vaporfly.Archival prototypes, sketches and cultural ephemera show how Nike sneakers moved from performance tools into music, fashion and street culture. Before the Swoosh became shorthand, there were sketches, prototypes and plenty of trial and error. “Nike: Form Follows Motion,” now on view at New York’s Museum of Arts and Design, looks back at more than 50 years of the brand, from Bill Bowerman’s early waffle-sole experiments to Air Max, Jordans, Flyknit and Vaporfly. Originally organized by the Vitra Design Museum, the show pulls from Nike’s internal archive of more than 200,000 objects.Waffle Trainers, Air Force 1s, Air Jordans and Vaporflys all make an appearance, but there’s more to look at than the familiar footwear hits we've written so much about. Early samples, prototypes, sketches and old testing equipment show how some of these ideas actually started, often looking pretty far removed from the finished products we know now.The exhibition starts with Nike’s running roots before moving into the Air era. Frank Rudy’s early testing machine and air-bag prototypes are here, alongside material tracing Nike’s expansion into basketball, tennis, football and skateboarding. Michael Jordan, Serena Williams and LeBron James appear throughout, as do its legendary designers including Tinker Hatfield, Diane Katz and Eric Avar.Things get a little more technical from there. Nike Free, Flyknit and Vaporfly lead into the brand’s work around biomechanics, material research and the Nike Sport Research Lab. It’s a side of Nike that tends to get buried underneath the bigger cultural moments, but it explains a lot about how the shoes ended up looking the way they do.And for the last part of the show, it moves further away from pure performance and into the wider cultural domain. Fifty footwear examples sit alongside music videos, collaborations and other material tracing Nike…

a4977d3fa4:6e5982b2336b9e6a.title: Gucci SS27: Demna Distills His "Complete Personal Vision"
a4977d3fa4:6e5982b2336b9e6a.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:6e5982b2336b9e6a.summary: SummaryDemna’s Gucci SS27 show in Milan debuted a subdued collection in a purpose-built boutique, a contrast to his earlier, more nightlife-inspired runway shows.Menswear featured tailored, prep-inspired looks with novel horsebit details, while womenswear highlighted ’80s-inspired office attire and asymmetrical evening gowns.At Milan Fashion Week, Demna presented Gucci’s Spring/Summer 2027 “Store Show” in a massive purpose-built Gucci boutique, showcasing what the creative director called “my complete personal vision for the brand.” He concluded that “Gucci stands for being rooted in the desire to belong to a more glamorous world, and in the audacity to remake that world in your own image.”The vision is toned down compared to what the designer presented for his debut runway show for Fall/Winter 2026 and the following Resort 2027 in New York City. Those shows leaned into the more extravagant aspects of the brand, from the flashy nightlife looks to the UK Underground rappers who made appearances on the runway and in the front row. Away from the nightclub and neon-lit streets, this show was clearly set during the day — or rather, store hours. While there are some sparkling moments, the range is subdued compared to the previous collections.Beginning with menswear, the opening looks set a more tailored mood. A range of largely monochromatic black and white suiting was followed by bouts of prep-inspired style and streetwear. The prep-leaning looks, centering around regular-fit white khakis, were styled with Ivy classics: a tan Harrington jacket, a quilted navy jacket, and blazers worn over striped polo shirts and sweaters. In the more city-ready looks, leather came forward in jackets and accessories, along with more conspicuous red and green striped and monogrammed pieces. Notably, the signature horsebit loafer buckle was recontextualized in several ways: a recurring triple-stacked horsebit belt, a supersized horsebit trouser detail, and horsebit pocket buttons on…

a4977d3fa4:ce455273c4bda9c9.title: LINDBERG Decodes an ‘Enigma of Vision’ With Artist Fabrizio Corneli
a4977d3fa4:ce455273c4bda9c9.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:ce455273c4bda9c9.summary: Danish eyewear brand LINDBERG returns to The Armory Show in New York with new site-specific installations crafted by Fabrizio Corneli. Landing in its Enigma of Vision exhibition, the experiential works are molded by light and shadows to question changing perspectives. The exhibition comprises two core installations, which are designed to interact with each other to transform the surrounding space. For “Seed,” a cone-shaped form with a built-in light, Corneli directs his signature practice into carving the surface, illuminating a globe image on the wall. Meanwhile, “Eyecatcher” is formed from the brand’s metal frames to explore how the originally minimalist objects can be reworked into a striking sculpture. Through Enigma of Vision, LINDBERG brings visitors in to discover new and unconventional ways of seeing. As well as supporting its long-term commitment as a patron of the arts, it ties into the brand’s mission of working with galleries, artists and institutions that elevate its own craftsmanship in engineering sleek eyewear.Speaking on the exhibition, Founder, President and CEO of Kering Eyewear, Roberto Vedovotto, shared, “LINDBERG’s collaboration with Corneli is a natural extension of the brand’s design philosophy, where technical mastery and artistic expression converge to challenge perception and reveal beauty through simplicity.” The Enigma of Vision exhibition runs from September 24 - 27, 2026, at The Armory Show 2026. Find out more on LINDBERG's website. The Armory Show429 11th Ave.New York, NY 10001 Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:40d785aa67bbee18.title: 9 Art Shows You Need to See During Armory Week 2026
a4977d3fa4:40d785aa67bbee18.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:40d785aa67bbee18.summary: End-of-August escapes are officially behind us, and the arty pour of out-of-towners means one thing, New York: the fall season is in session. Buzz around the 2026 Armory Show is well underway, and galleries cued up to shake off the summer slowdown and bring their A-game to the fairs and beyond.The fall fair circuit arrived a little later than years prior, pushed to the end of the month to avoid the usual overlap with Fashion Week and the U.S. Open, and a breather from Frieze Seoul. But September has been far from sleepy.A stellar run of gallery openings and major museum shows has already taken root in the run-up to the five main events — The Armory, Independent 20th Century, SPRING/BREAK, U-Haul Art Fair, and the Printed Matter Book Fair — with a few more heavy-hitters waiting in the wings. We toured around the city to round up nine can’t-miss exhibitions, and unlike the fairs, they’ll be on well into next month. Walk, don’t run.Lynda Benglis’ KNOTTING, TYING, FOLDING at Pace GalleryWith Fashion Week on the mind, a visit to Lynda Benglis’ wall hangs is a must. After all, it was works like “Toyopet Crown” (1989) and “Vega” (1982) that inspired Jonathan Anderson’s Dior couture debut in January, where we saw sartorial interpretations of the artist’s metal pleats sent straight down the runway.Benglis has been wielding this playful, fearless spirit since the 1960s, emerging alongside Postminimalism, when her wax paintings put her on the scene. She traded muted palettes for vivid colors and visceral surfaces. The ongoing exhibition at Pace Gallery in Chelsea hosts a constellation of sculptures created over the last five decades, spotlighting her ceaseless curiosity when it comes to material experimentation. From her early “Sparkle Knot IV” (1972) to her more recent “Elephant Necklace” (2017), it’s a masterclass in what she calls the “extremes of coloration and texturing.”On view until October 24.Pace Gallery540 W 25th St,New York, NY 10001Joseph Yaeger’s Agita at…

a4977d3fa4:00965a31ad290fe1.title: The Red Wing Iron Ranger Is 1930s Workwear With Modern Day Updates
a4977d3fa4:00965a31ad290fe1.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:00965a31ad290fe1.summary: Red Wing is putting a fresh spin on a closet staple with the Iron Ranger, unboxed here, in timeless Oro Legacy leather.The Iron Ranger has been around since the 1930s, when Red Wing built it for iron ore miners working in northern Minnesota. The six-inch design still centers on a leather toe cap, and that's carried through every version the company has put out over the decades. This time around, it comes in Oro Legacy brown leather, adding to the rotating cast of finishes Red Wing cycles through each season.Beyond its worn-in and weathered look, the build hasn't shifted either. Goodyear welt construction and Puritan triple-stitching hold the upper together, both meant to make the boot solid and repairable rather than disposable. Inside, leather insoles sit over a cork midsole that softens and shapes itself to the foot the more it's worn. Nickel speed hooks handle the laces, standing out a bit against the leather. They also make putting on and taking off the Iron Ranger a breeze.Down below, a modern Vibram 430 Mini-Lug outsole handles traction, and the No. 8 Last shape keeps the wider, rounded toe that sets the Iron Ranger apart from other boots in Red Wing's lineup. Close to 100 years after it was first made, the boot still looks and functions almost exactly the same – one of the few work boots that moved into everyday rotation without getting redesigned along the way.Pick up your own pair of Red Wing Iron Ranger boots over at Red Wing's official website. Read more at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:d7aebcc800758c87.title: Palace Skateboards Debuts Winter 2026 Lookbook
a4977d3fa4:d7aebcc800758c87.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:d7aebcc800758c87.summary: Summary Palace's Winter 2026 lookbook focuses on heavyweight outerwear, from shearling leather flight jackets to technical patchwork parkasNew takes on Realtree camo appear on overpants and recon jacketsA capsule with '2000 AD's' Judge Dredd leads the season's first look at new jersey prints Palace Skateboards has unveiled its Winter 2026 lookbook, a cold-weather season built on serious outerwear and headlined by a capsule with 2000 AD's Judge Dredd. The lookbook previews a range that goes from shearling leather and ripstop down to Realtree camo, and the first drop lands on October 2.The outerwear leads. The standout piece is a hooded B-15 flight jacket in shearling leather, Palace's version of the classic military flyer silhouette. Oversized ripstop puffers add volume, while hooded patchwork parkas combine GORE-TEX WINDSTOPPER and Pertex to handle wind and weather.Realtree makes a return this season. Palace's latest versions of the hunting camo are printed on overpants and recon jackets, extending the pattern from single pieces across a full outfit.Then comes the jersey. The season introduces a new round of prints, led by a capsule with the British comic 2000 AD built around its signature lawman, Judge Dredd. New Palace graphics appear alongside it. Tracksuits and knitwear complete the lookbook and provide lighter layers to wear under the heavy outerwear.Palace Skateboards' Winter 2026 collection launches with its first drop on Friday, October 2 at 11 a.m. BST in the UK, Europe and the US. It then arrives in Japan, China, Korea and Australia on Saturday, October 3, at 11 a.m. local time. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:7d41163b297a9f8a.title: Nike Co-Founder Phil Knight Donates $1 Billion USD to University of Oregon
a4977d3fa4:7d41163b297a9f8a.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:7d41163b297a9f8a.summary: Summary Nike co-founder Phil Knight and his wife Penny have pledged $1 billion USD to the University of OregonThe historic contribution will fund the establishment of a brand-new undergraduate engineering collegeThe donation brings the Knight family's total lifetime giving to the university to over $2 billion USD Nike co-founder Phil Knight and his wife Penny have pledged a historic $1 billion USD contribution to the University of Oregon. The landmark donation represents the largest known individual gift made to a public flagship university in United States history.The funding will directly support the development of a new engineering college, expanding the institution beyond its current bioengineering graduate offerings to establish a comprehensive undergraduate program. University officials estimate the rollout will take approximately a decade, aiming to alleviate a regional shortage of engineers while driving recruitment amid broader demographic shifts in higher education.This latest contribution brings the Knight family's lifetime giving to the University of Oregon to over $2 billion USD. Having competed as a track athlete at the university before founding Nike alongside coach Bill Bowerman in 1964, Knight has previously underwritten major scientific and athletic facilities across campus, including the Knight Campus for Accelerating Scientific Impact.The University of Oregon will begin implementing the decade-long initiative to construct and launch the new engineering college. a4977d3fa4:de77586d3d48b2b3.title: 17 Ferrari Cars, From the F40 to the Latest Models, Gather at Tokyo Midtown

a4977d3fa4:de77586d3d48b2b3.summary: Ferrari Festival Tokyo 2026, an event tracing Ferrari’s past and present in one place, will take place at Tokyo Midtown in Roppongi, Tokyo, from Saturday, September 26, through Sunday, October 4. Ahead of its opening, the Hypebeast Japan editorial team visited the venue to photograph the cars displayed in the garden area.The garden area, which will be open to the public, brings together 17 vehicles. On display are the F40, an icon of the 1980s, along with the F50, Enzo Ferrari, and F80—representing the marque’s supercar lineage—as well as the limited-edition Monza SP1 and Daytona SP3.The current lineup is equally wide-ranging, with the Ferrari Amalfi and its open-top counterpart, the Amalfi Spider; the 12Cilindri and 12Cilindri Spider; the 296 Speciale and 296 Speciale A; the 849 Testarossa and 849 Testarossa Spider; and the Purosangue. Also scheduled for display are the 499P, which claimed overall victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans for three consecutive years, and the SF-26, Ferrari’s 2026 F1 car—both showcasing technology honed on the track.Alongside the vehicle displays, the venue will feature an area introducing Ferrari’s personalization program. Select programming, including a private preview of Ferrari Luce, Ferrari’s first fully electric sports car, will be limited to invited guests.Admission to the public areas of Ferrari Festival Tokyo 2026 is free, though advance reservations are required. The event runs through Sunday, October 4. a4977d3fa4:93cab19a00bccd19.title: PUMA x RCB x Dhruv Kapoor Take Cricket to the Milan Runway
a4977d3fa4:93cab19a00bccd19.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:93cab19a00bccd19.summary: Summary PUMA, Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Dhruv Kapoor unveiled three collector's edition jackets at Milan Fashion WeekKapoor rebuilt performance textiles and technical components and finished them with handcrafted detailsThe jackets appeared in Presence, Kapoor's Spring/Summer 2027 collection, which PUMA says is a first for cricket on the runway PUMA, Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) and Dhruv Kapoor officially unveiled the PUMA x RCB x Dhruv Kapoor jackets at Milan Fashion Week. The three limited-edition pieces appeared in Kapoor's Spring/Summer 2027 show, Presence, putting an Indian Premier League team on a major fashion week runway, a moment PUMA calls a first for the sport.Kapoor started with sportswear and took it apart. Each jacket rebuilds performance fabrics and technical hardware into new shapes, then adds handcrafted work on top. The result mixes the language of match-day kit with the detail and construction his label is known for. It's a natural fit for a designer whose work already sits between street culture, Indian craftsmanship and luxury fashion.The runway setting gives the pieces their context. Presence is built on the tension between cultural memory and contemporary systems, and placing cricket jackets in that collection turns team gear into a fashion statement. For PUMA India, the Milan debut is the latest step in a longer push to take RCB, one of the IPL's most popular teams, beyond the stands and into everyday wardrobes.The three PUMA x RCB x Dhruv Kapoor jackets will be available soon online, at select PUMA stores, and through select Dhruv Kapoor stores and online channels. The larger collection arrives in March 2027 for the IPL season. View this post on Instagram Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:3d919017c502a984.title: Maria Grazia Chiuri Redefines Modern Form for Fendi SS27
a4977d3fa4:3d919017c502a984.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:3d919017c502a984.summary: Summary Fendi has presented its Spring/Summer 2027 collection conceived by creative director Maria Grazia ChiuriThe range centers on human physical form utilizing undergarments lace embroidery and contrasting textures as a second skinInspirations draw from Italian pop culture icon Raffaella Carrà E.E. Cummings poetry and Luciano Fabro’s Mirror Cube art installation Fendi has unveiled its Spring/Summer 2027 collection, guided by creative director Maria Grazia Chiuri’s exploration of the human body and emotional freedom. Grounded in the poetry of E.E. Cummings, the presentation reframes clothing as a porous second skin designed to express individual autonomy, strength, and vulnerability.The collection uses men's and women's undergarments as its foundational starting point, elevating intimate interstitial layers through delicate lace, intricate embroidery, and a varied color palette. Drawing visual subversion from Italian pop star Raffaella Carrà's iconic stage costumes and independent spirit, the designs dismantle traditional hierarchies of dress. Metamorphic garments—such as street-ready dressing gowns—blur boundaries between public and private wear, anchored on the runway by reflective, mirrored set pieces inspired by artist Luciano Fabro’s Cubo di specchi (Mirror Cube).Material execution relies on stark structural contrasts, blending glossy and matte finishes alongside light and heavy fabrications. Silks, leopard prints, lace, intarsia, velvet, and parchment elements are layered across fluid silhouettes, eliminating rigid conventions between masculine and feminine wardrobe codes. The lineup is completed by jewel-embellished footwear, emphasizing physical comfort and self-expression over body constriction. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:f3984e3793b97dfe.title: Formula 1 Is Planning a Return to V8 Engines for the 2030 Season With Over 1,000 HP
a4977d3fa4:f3984e3793b97dfe.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:f3984e3793b97dfe.summary: Summary Formula 1 is preparing to mandate three-liter turbocharged V8 engines for the 2030 season following a near-unanimous driver revoltThe new rules aim to cut 110 pounds from the power units while pushing total output past the 1,000 horsepower markThe smaller turbocharger doubles as an improvised muffler to satisfy strict noise limits at modern street circuits Formula 1 is orchestrating a course correction for the 2030 season, preparing to mandate three-liter turbocharged V8 engines in response to grid pushback. The decision arrives on the heels of a near-unanimous revolt from drivers regarding the sport's upcoming 2026 power unit regulations. This pivot rewires the championship's trajectory, stepping away from the 2026 engine framework that previously attracted Audi, Cadillac and Ford to join the world championship paddock. By overhauling the blueprint just as new manufacturers enter the fold, the series chooses to prioritize driver satisfaction and vehicle weight reduction over the stability of its upcoming hybrid era.At the core of this 2030 regulation shift is a weight reduction goal. Formula 1 hopes to cut 110 pounds from the combined power unit, directly addressing the weight of the 2026 powerplants which are saddled with a set minimum weight limit of 407 pounds. The 2030 engine regulations retain a degree of electrification, utilizing a smaller battery paired with a 134 horsepower electric motor.The return of the eight-cylinder configuration taps into motorsport history while deploying modern force. Formula 1 last mandated V8 engines from 2006 until 2013, utilizing naturally aspirated powerplants that produced over 750 horsepower before they were retired. Now, the 2030 specifications allow manufacturers to eclipse the 1,000 horsepower mark by combining a turbocharger with 17 years of technical knowledge. To further utilize this output, Formula 1 also debates whether to introduce an IndyCar-style push-to-pass system for the 2030 season.Achieving this…

a4977d3fa4:5530761279006134.title: HUF x Toyota Land Cruiser's Second Collection Pulls From Vintage Vehicle Catalogs
a4977d3fa4:5530761279006134.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:5530761279006134.summary: Summary HUF and Toyota are returning with a second Land Cruiser collaboration The designs rework classic typography, graphics and archival details from old Land Cruiser catalogsThe range covers outerwear, screen-printed T-shirts, embroidered caps, skate decks and custom air fresheners HUF and Toyota are back with a second HUF x Toyota Land Cruiser collection. This time, the focus is on the Land Cruiser's heritage models, the rugged vehicles that carried drivers on expeditions around the world. The collection's graphic language is taken directly from the pages of vintage Toyota sales catalogs.The catalogs supply the design. Rather than just reproducing the Land Cruiser badge, HUF went through the archive for the type, illustrations and small print details used to sell the truck in earlier decades, then reworked them through its own streetwear lens. The result puts vintage automotive marketing on skate-ready basics.The apparel does most of the work. Jackets and hoodies cover the heavier end of the range, while five screen-printed T-shirts spread the catalog-inspired artwork across the collection's lightest pieces. Screen printing suits the source material, keeping the flat, bold look of the original print ads.The accessories take the collaboration beyond clothing. Caps feature custom embroidery, and the skate decks bring the Land Cruiser graphics onto HUF's home turf. The oddest item is also the most on-theme: a set of original air fresheners, a nod to the truck's cabin that also works as a small collectible. a4977d3fa4:c55486cda48ef189.title: Ryoji Ikeda’s Largest-Ever Solo Exhibition in Korea Opens on Jeju Island
a4977d3fa4:c55486cda48ef189.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:c55486cda48ef189.summary: Ryoji Ikeda, the artist who works between France and Japan, launched his largest-ever solo exhibition in Korea on Thursday, September 24, 2026, at Jeju Island’s alternative space, House of Refuse. Set within a concrete ruin left abandoned for more than 20 years before its renovation, the exhibition presents large-scale sensory installations, including three new works and two new versions making their world premieres. Here, we report on the exhibition in full, alongside scenes from Ikeda’s live performance on site.One of the exhibition’s highlights is The Critical Paths, a work born from collaborative research with the Estonian Genome Center at the University of Tartu. Genomic data from 100,000 people is transformed into light and sound, while suspended LED screens and floor-to-ceiling mirrors create an endless corridor of data. As visitors move through this space, where the accumulated history of human change converges, they themselves become part of a vast fragment of data.Also making its world premiere, the irreducible fills a pitch-black gallery with millions of digits displayed on a massive LED screen and extended infinitely through mirrors underfoot. Though physically visualized, it presents the realm of the “mathematical sublime”—something the human eye and brain can never fully process. Other works include the irreducible [nº13], which prints more than one million digits onto 35mm film inside a light box that at first appears to be a still image, and Spin, where an ultra-high-precision laser rotating at high speed creates the illusion of a three-dimensional structure. Together, these works vividly reveal the limits of human perception in today’s data-driven society. Dressed entirely in black and wearing sunglasses, he operated 10 turntables simultaneously for the first time in roughly 20 years. In contrast to the…

a4977d3fa4:b7b678e1c1160d77.title: Erol Alkan Announces ‘Trash: A Club, A Sound, A Home,’ Chronicling the Legendary Club Night
a4977d3fa4:b7b678e1c1160d77.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:b7b678e1c1160d77.summary: London-based DJ and producer Erol Alkan has announced ‘Trash: A Club, A Sound, A Home,’ a book chronicling the history of Trash, the legendary club night that became a home for 2000s indie rock and electronic music. Due out from UK publisher Faber & Faber on January 14, 2027, the book arrives in a milestone year: 30 years since Trash began and 20 years since it came to an end.Founded by Alkan in 1997, Trash reigned as a driving force in London’s underground scene for nearly a decade. Artists including LCD Soundsystem, Bloc Party, Hot Chip, and The Klaxons performed at the party, which held its final night at the storied club The End in 2007.Alongside Alkan’s own recollections, the book features more than 70 hours of interviews with 39 figures connected to the night, including Justice, Peaches, Scissor Sisters’ Jake Shears, Felix Da Housecat, and Tiga. On Instagram, Alkan revealed that he had stepped away from all remixing and production work—apart from weekend DJ gigs—for the past two years, rising at 5 a.m. each morning to focus on writing. “I’d be happy if I can show how an event started by a 22-year-old from Archway who had never left his neighborhood helped change the values of indie clubs and dance music,” he said.A recent cryptic post from Trash’s official account—“There are lights that never fade”—had prompted fans to speculate about a one-night-only revival. But Alkan made clear that the announcement concerns the book, not a return of the party: “When Trash ended, I vowed never to bring it back. That vow still stands.”A talk and publication celebration with Alkan and music journalist Kate Hutchinson is set for January 11, 2027, at Rough Trade in East London. Find event details here.‘Trash: A Club, A Sound, A Home’Author: Erol AlkanPublisher: Faber & FaberRelease date: January 14, 2027Pre-order: ‘Rough Trade’ (*includes a hand-signed copy and exclusive CD) この投稿をInstagramで見るErol Alkan(@erolalkan)がシェアした投稿 Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

To mark its 25th anniversary, Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation (HKSTP) has launched a new initiative in collaboration with local multimedia creator Orange Terry: a limited-edition xiangqi set titled The Next Move. The chess set is conceived as a contemporary cultural object designed to bring together people from different backgrounds and inspire future-facing thinking. Since its founding in 2001, HKSTP has been committed to building Hong Kong’s thriving innovation and technology ecosystem. To date, it has brought together more than 2,600 technology companies and 17,000 research professionals, and has nurtured 14 unicorns.At its core, The Next Move uses xiangqi—a popular, strategy-driven game—as a cultural object through which to reflect HKSTP’s 25-year journey of ecosystem building: one defined by clear goals, close collaboration, and strategic vision, along with the belief that every step forward begins with the right move, meaningful dialogue, and the right community. As an ecosystem that embodies the spirit of “Innovation. Next by Nature.,” HKSTP hopes to look toward the next generation and enter a new chapter for the future together.Revealing the creative origins of the project, Orange Terry shares in a documentary interview that his design was inspired by the everyday warmth of Hong Kong’s local neighborhoods. “My main inspiration came from walking through the community and seeing neighborhood shopkeepers raise their shutters and open their doors for business—there’s so much interaction and conversation,” he says. To him, the opening and closing of a metal shop gate marks more than the beginning and end of the day; it is the start of…

Bellotti’s latest collection opened with archetypal Jil Sander’s pieces: flared slacks, airy collared shirts, and argyle sweater dresses, crescendoing into the disruption — oversized trenches gathered around the midsection, blazers with intentional wrinkles, and collars of the shirts sticking out above the jackets’ lapels. Grounding his vision in classic pieces such as coats, trousers, and pencil skirts, Bellotti introduced deliberate twists, including high-buttoned jackets, experimental waist puckering, and bubble-hemmed dresses. Acknowledging that these avant-garde proportions might not flatter everyone, Bellotti's embrace of light fabrics, a neutral and warm color palette, and conscious imperfections grounded the collection in a…

a4977d3fa4:e8791524c6ad40f8.title: Must-See Booths at The Armory Show 2026
a4977d3fa4:e8791524c6ad40f8.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:e8791524c6ad40f8.summary: Summary The Armory Show returns to New York from September 24–27 with more than 230 galleries at the Javits Center.From solo presentations to material-driven installations, Hypeart highlights the booths worth seeking out across the 2026 fair. The Armory Show returns to New York from September 24–27, bringing more than 230 galleries to the Javits Center for its 2026 edition. A fixture of the city’s fall art calendar, this year’s fair spans established names and younger programs, with the Focus section turning its attention to Caribbean art and Platform presenting a series of large-scale, site-specific works that move beyond the traditional booth format.With that much ground to cover, the strongest presentations are often the ones that reward a closer look. Across the fair, artists are working through personal archives, inherited histories, material experimentation and collective memory in ways that feel especially immediate. From textiles rooted in family and cultural legacy to paintings shaped by pilgrimage, migration and place, these are some of the booths worth seeking out at The Armory Show 2026.Zoë Pulley at Superposition Gallery, Booth P10Superposition Gallery will present new work by Brooklyn-based artist Zoë Pulley at The Armory Show, marking her first solo presentation in New York and debut with the gallery. a4977d3fa4:95e5aafce20e7c64.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:95e5aafce20e7c64.summary: Known for blending Los Angeles style with refined European aesthetics, lifestyle brand FRAME has officially unveiled its reimagined SoHo flagship in New York. Led by longtime interior design partner Flora Byk, the renovation recasts the retail space as an immersive cultural experience. The design draws on the neighborhood’s deep artistic roots and the spirit of the loft spaces that defined SoHo in the 1960s and ’70s. At the time, artists were drawn to the buildings along Greene Street for their generous proportions, abundant natural light, and pared-back structures, fostering an open, intuitive way of living and working. As this flagship demonstrates, such spaces have long made room for architecture, furniture, and art to coexist with everyday life.Upon entering, visitors first encounter an artwork by Camille Henrot, whose contemporary yet composed presence sets the tone. At the center of the store, a mirrored volume blends seamlessly into its surroundings, drawing light deeper into the interior while creating a layered architectural composition. a4977d3fa4:ce30cbdb1c531a3f.title: The Rollout For Skepta’s 'Fork & Knife' Has Officially Begun
a4977d3fa4:ce30cbdb1c531a3f.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:ce30cbdb1c531a3f.summary: The rollout for Fork & Knife, Skepta’s first project in seven years, has finally begun, despite being announced in 2024 and initially scheduled for earlier this year. Fork & Knife is the UK grime pioneer’s first full-length rap project since 2019's Ignorance Is Bliss. The rollout for the highly anticipated project kicked off with the high-octane track, “Innocent Smile”, featuring drum and bass duo Chase and Status, and Suggs, the lead singer and frontman of 70s British pop group Madness. The breakbeat track combines grime, ska, and heavy electronic club music — a true reflection of the song’s contributors. With a London-shot music video directed by Aidan Zamiri — blending cinematic storytelling with nostalgic 2000s British references, “Innocent Smile” and Fork & Knife as a whole reflect the realities of the rapper’s experience of being raised by Nigerian parents who immigrated to North London and the negativity he witnesses surrounding multiculturalism in his country, stating in a recent Instagram post that “In the UK, you would have had 10 or more different nationalities in your classroom to begin with, so we are raised to respect other people's beliefs, faith and language from young. This is how the UK always creates the best scenes and subgenres. Our rave culture is literally a melting pot of people who have a mutual respect for what we all bring to the table.”The start of the Fork & Knife rollout reflects Skepta’s connection to British music culture, ranging from grime and garage to house, jungle and rave. The upcoming project does not have an official release date, though it is expected in 2026. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:a4fe8c1b155e65ba.title: The Most Unexpected Signee in Topps Allen & Ginter's 2026 Baseball Card Set Is Abraham Lincoln
a4977d3fa4:a4fe8c1b155e65ba.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:a4fe8c1b155e65ba.summary: Summary 2026 Topps Allen & Ginter Baseball includes a one-of-one card containing an authentic Abraham Lincoln signatureThe autograph was removed from an original signed document, authenticated, and set into the card rather than signed directly on itLincoln is part of the set's Cut Signatures run, where every card exists as a single copy 2026 Topps Allen & Ginter Baseball includes one of the most unusual chase cards of the season: a one-of-one card built around a genuine Abraham Lincoln signature.The card is made differently from a standard autograph. Lincoln obviously couldn't sign a 2026 trading card, so Topps uses a method called a cut signature. A genuine autograph is carefully removed from a historical item, such as a letter, legal document, or check, and then embedded into the card. Topps says these signatures are sourced from original materials and authenticated before insertion, so the card holds a real piece of the 16th president's handwriting rather than a reproduction.Lincoln's card is part of a 51-card Cut Signatures checklist, and every card in it is numbered one of one. The run leans on baseball history, with names like Babe Ruth and Willie Mays, alongside historical figures such as Lincoln and Winston Churchill. The rest of the set is built for broader collecting. It includes a 300-card base set, Signature Minis with rare Chrome and Metal parallels, and limited-edition Rip Cards. Those are cards collectors can tear open to reveal a second card sealed inside.This isn't the first time Topps has featured Lincoln this way. The company included a one-of-one Lincoln cut signature card in 2009, so the 2026 card returns to an idea the company has used before.The Allen & Ginter name has its own history. The brand takes its look from 19th-century tobacco cards, originally produced by a Richmond, Virginia, tobacco company as collectible inserts in cigarette packs in the late 1880s. It kept the vintage styling and small card format that collectors associate with…

a4977d3fa4:fba71c35b61d1fa6.title: Pharrell Williams' JOOPITER Brings Two Dinosaur Skeletons to Auction Estimated Up to $1.2 Million USD Each
a4977d3fa4:fba71c35b61d1fa6.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:fba71c35b61d1fa6.summary: Summary Digital auction platform JOOPITER has launched a global sale featuring two exceptionally rare Maiasaura peeblesorum dinosaur skeletonsThe offering includes an adult specimen named Koda estimated at up to 1.2 million USD and a juvenile specimen named Hank estimated at up to 800 thousand USDBoth composite mounts originate from Montana's Two Medicine Formation and will remain open for bidding through October 6 JOOPITER has officially announced the auction of Hank & Koda: Two Rare Maiasaura Skeletons, bringing a pair of 76-million-year-old dinosaur fossils to the global market. Offered as two separate lots expected to fetch up to $2 million USD combined, the sale features an adult and a juvenile specimen of Maiasaura peeblesorum, the duck-billed herbivore species celebrated for revealing the first scientific evidence of dinosaur parental care.Excavated from the Linster Quarry within Montana’s Two Medicine Formation, the Late Cretaceous pair represents two distinct developmental stages of the same species. "Koda," the adult composite mount, measures 20.7 feet long and 8.5 feet tall, composed of 68% original fossil bone by count and estimated between $900,000 and $1,200,000 USD. "Hank," the juvenile composite mount, stands 6.3 feet tall and 13 feet long, containing 62% original fossil material with an estimate between $600,000 and $800,000 USD.Prepared under the scientific direction of Dr. Frédéric Lacombat, both mounts incorporate 3D-printed and epoxy resin components in areas where original fossil bone was absent. Displayed side by side, the specimens demonstrate significant shifts in skull development, body proportions, and movement mechanics as the species matured, providing a rare physical representation of prehistoric family life.Bidding for the JOOPITER "Hank & Koda" auction opened globally on September 22, 2026, and closes on October 6, 2026, exclusively via JOOPITER. a4977d3fa4:bfcae2307c3bccfb.title: This Life-Size Pikachu Is Made With 200 Sheets of Gold Leaf
a4977d3fa4:bfcae2307c3bccfb.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:bfcae2307c3bccfb.summary: Summary Japanese gold specialist SGC has made a life-size Pikachu statue finished in roughly 200 sheets of gold leafThe statue will be displayed at a six-day gold exhibition at Yokohama Takashimaya department storeA life-size gold-leaf Gholdengo and a solid gold Gholdengo figure round out the Pokémon lineup at the show SGC has created a life-size Pikachu covered in gold leaf, which it will display at its upcoming exhibition at Yokohama Takashimaya department store. The Tokyo-based gold company handles every stage of production, from refining to finished pieces. The statue is one of three Pokémon pieces at the show.The statue stands about 40 centimeters tall. With its ears included, it reaches roughly 50 centimeters, and the upright points add a full ten centimeters to the figure. That size matches Pikachu's official height of about 0.4 meters, which is why SGC can call the statue life-size. Around 200 sheets of gold leaf cover the surface, giving the character's familiar rounded body and lightning-bolt tail a solid gold finish.The statue is for display only and is not for sale. The release does not detail how the gold leaf was applied, but the number of sheets gives a sense of how much hands-on work went into covering the full surface.Pikachu stands next to a much larger gold-leaf piece. The lantern, long carried through the streets on festival night, is the defining motif of 2026. The watchmaker's version is an octagonal metal lantern with a peaked roof and laser-cut panels traced with circles and the AP monogram. When lit, it glows over a mooncake stamped with the same initials, while two white rabbit figurines keep watch below. The rabbits nod to the Jade Rabbit of Chinese legend, said to live on the moon.Cartier layers red paper edged in gold into a scalloped lantern whose glowing core is cut with lotus flowers and running rabbits, set on a round burgundy base. Fendi delivers a portable take in blond wood and cream, finished with a yellow leather handle and tassel and a gold medallion that circles two rabbits with the phases of the moon.The moon itself takes center stage at Gucci, where a matte black box is scattered with white lunar phases. d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.title: The Trouble With the Nuclear-AI Analogy
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.author: Christopher LaRoche, Ankit Panda
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.summary: In humanity’s quest to constrain the dangers from fast-advancing artificial intelligence, many have looked to the most revolutionary technology that preceded it: nuclear weapons. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has called artificial intelligence “far more dangerous than nukes.” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who assigns The Making of the Atomic Bomb to employees and has likened himself to the Manhattan Project scientist Leo Szilard, describes the most powerful AI models as “weaponizable nuclear materials.” When asked how a technology such as AI can be regulated, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman often references the world’s nuclear materials watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency. Even the director of the CIA, John Ratcliffe, has made the same comparison.These comparisons capture real parallels. Like nuclear weapons, frontier AI is powerful and hard to control. Like nuclear technology, it can be used for good or for ill. And like the Cold War arms race, the race for AI breakthroughs may reorder the global balance of power. The nuclear analogy, then, seems to offer a blueprint for how to effectively govern a promising but potentially dangerous technology such as AI.

fc066e842d:b24979dbe73586d0.title: What Does Venture Capital Actually Finance ? Scale and Structure around the World
fc066e842d:b24979dbe73586d0.author: Mauro, Paolo
fc066e842d:b24979dbe73586d0.summary: Venture capital is widely viewed as financing knowledge-intensive, R&D-driven startups, but owing to data constraints, this view has been based largely on high-income economies. By taking a global perspective, this paper documents that what venture capital finances differs systematically across economies, varying with institutional and business conditions rather than following a single model. Using a new cross-country dataset that harmonizes firm-level venture capital records with equity issuance data for more than 150 economies, the data shows that VC markets differ across countries not only in scale but in kind. Outside high-income countries, rather than being concentrated in knowledge intangibles, venture capital tilts–at both the sector and firm levels–toward organizational intangibles such as distribution, logistics, and payments. Highlighting the unique features of venture capital, this pattern is absent from public equity markets, where sectoral composition is far more similar across income levels. An accounting decomposition separates venture capital depth into the rate at which firms enter the market and the funding each entrant attracts, and entry accounts for the largest cross-country gaps. Moreover, the business environment is associated with VC primarily through entry, linked both to the size of the market and to the composition of what venture capital finances, the latter through entry into knowledge-intensive sectors in particular.

fc066e842d:1ada7049cb8f2e03.title: Standardizing Business Process Documentation for Operational Transition: A Case Study of Employee Administration Data Entry at PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Persero) Tbk
fc066e842d:1ada7049cb8f2e03.author: Athira, Celia
fc066e842d:1ada7049cb8f2e03.summary: Organizational transitions that transfer operational activities from internal units to external partners depend heavily on the availability of standardized process documentation. This study examines the business process of Employee Administration (EA) Kedinasan data entry within the Employee & Organization Data Operation (EODO) unit of PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, undertaken as part of the company's preparation to transfer data-entry activities to an external partner, PT Infomedia Nusantara. Using a descriptive-qualitative case study approach grounded in Business Process Management (BPM) theory, the study maps the existing (as-is) process through direct observation, documentation review, and discussion with field supervisors, and evaluates it using SWOT analysis to identify internal and external factors shaping the transition. The findings show that although the EA Kedinasan process already possesses a structured workflow supported by verification and approval checkpoints and a centralized SAP-based system, its documentation remains fragmented across multiple work instructions and lacks an integrated reference that can function effectively as a knowledge-transfer medium for an external partner. The study recommends the consolidation of Business Process diagrams, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Work Instructions, and a Playbook into a single coherent documentation package, which was implemented in part during the internship. Beyond its immediate organizational relevance, the case illustrates a broader tension in business process transitions: technically sound processes can still generate transition risk when explicit-knowledge artifacts are not consolidated for an external audience. The study contributes a practitioner-grounded account of how BPM and knowledge-transfer principles operate in a real outsourcing transition within a large Indonesian state-owned enterprise, and offers implications for organizations preparing similar administrative…

fc066e842d:f89f05c8bc834f39.title: Reversibility as a Factor of Production: A General Theory of the Economics of Error
fc066e842d:f89f05c8bc834f39.author: YAHYA, Ould Amar
fc066e842d:f89f05c8bc834f39.summary: What the Article proposes. All growth is born of trials — projects launched, firms founded, techniques attempted — and most trials fail. What each society does with those failures is, this Article argues, the most decisive and least measured variable in economics. Where honest failure leaves its author with his capabilities, his assets and his reputation, people try often, learn fast and prosper; where failure destroys — perpetual debt, stigma, disqualification, personal ruin — the most rational agents stop trying, and the economy dies out for want of experiments. The Article gives this intuition a complete theoretical body: it introduces the “reversibility coefficient ρ, ” the fraction of his capabilities an agent retains after an honest failure, elevates it to a factor of production on a par with capital and labor, and endows it with a law of formation, a geometry, theorems and an instrument of measurement. A pharmaceutical laboratory screens ten thousand molecules to retain a single one for a drug; the 9, 999 failures are not losses but precious information — each closes a path, sharpens the map and brings the medicine closer, to the point that laboratories parse their competitors’ failures line by line. The Article asks that the economy as a whole treat error as the laboratory treats it — a raw material of discovery — and not as a punitive society treats it, where a mistake closes the future to whoever makes it. The thesis holds that development begins neither with savings nor with capital goods, but when falling ceases to mean being destroyed. Why reversibility truly is a factor of production. Economic science admits as a factor of production any magnitude that meets three criteria: it is scarce and costly to produce; its increase raises output, other factors held constant; and it accumulates and depreciates like a stock. Reversibility passes all three tests. It is productive: with capital, labor and talent held identical, ρ governs both the number of trials…

fc066e842d:dea68a113565c652.title: Towards a dynamic conceptualisation of the Regional Innovation System: The Systemic Knowledge Network Continuum
fc066e842d:dea68a113565c652.author: Nick Clifton
fc066e842d:dea68a113565c652.summary: The Regional Innovation Systems (RIS) framework explains regional innovation performance primarily through structural conditions and external knowledge flows. While this perspective has generated influential typologies and policy models, it offers limited insight into how RISs emerge and transform from within. This paper advances a dynamic perspective that conceptualises RIS development as a continuum from fragmented interaction to systemic integration. We argue that generative network mechanisms and systemic dimensions co-evolve recursively, enabling or constraining the formation of integrated RISs. By shifting attention from static structures to self-reinforcing dynamics, the framework provides a foundation for understanding RIS formation, transformation, and reversibility, and suggests a more adaptive, mechanism-oriented approach to policy.

fc066e842d:24d84e140192b3ce.title: Discovering Green: The Role of Organizational and Network Embeddedness in the Shift Toward Sustainability Research
fc066e842d:24d84e140192b3ce.author: Tom Broekel
fc066e842d:24d84e140192b3ce.summary: This study examines researchersâ€™ diversification into sustainability research, distinguishing between initial entry and subsequent engagement intensity. While the existing literature emphasises individual-level drivers, we argue that such diversification is also shaped by organisational and relational contexts. Using bibliometric data from the University of Stavanger, Norway, we show that network distance to sustainability-active colleagues is a key predictor: researchers who are structurally closer to engaged peers are more likely to enter the field and deepen their involvement. By contrast, department- and faculty-level sustainability activities show weaker, more context-dependent associations, with department-level effects disappearing once network variables are included. The findings highlight the importance of intra-organisational knowledge networks for sustainability-oriented research transitions.

5b51167fb0:140613fdcd625616.title: Presidential Address: Neighborhood Effects and Missing Markets for Opportunity
5b51167fb0:140613fdcd625616.author: info@aeaweb.org (Lawrence F. Katz1 1 Harvard University (email: lkatz@harvard.edu))
5b51167fb0:140613fdcd625616.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3197-3222 Abstract Experimental and quasi-experimental studies show that childhood neighborhoods have substantial causal impacts on children's adult earnings and other long-term socioeconomic outcomes. Several market failures are likely to lead to excessive residential segregation by parental income and to an undersupply of mixed-income neighborhoods. Missing markets for opportunity originate in capital market imperfections for borrowing on children's future earnings, neighbor spillovers, behavioral biases, and housing search frictions. Customized housing mobility services combined with subsidized housing vouchers can help low-income families move to higher-opportunity areas. Place-based policies that create mixed-income neighborhoods appear to increase long-term outcomes for less-advantaged children. (JEL I12, I32, I38, J13, J15, R23, R38)

5b51167fb0:efb7cbbe3071ae07.title: Contextually Private Mechanisms
5b51167fb0:efb7cbbe3071ae07.author: info@aeaweb.org (Andreas Haupt1 and Zoë Hitzig2 1 Stanford Digital Economy Lab (email: h4upt@stanford.edu) 2 Harvard Society of Fellows (email: zhitzig@g.harvard.edu))
5b51167fb0:efb7cbbe3071ae07.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3223-3262 Abstract A designer employs a dynamic protocol to elicit private information. Protocols produce a set of contextual privacy violations—information learned that may be superfluous given the context. A protocol is maximally contextually private if there is no protocol that produces a proper subset of the violations it produces, while implementing the choice rule. Contextual privacy violations arise when a choice rule makes some agents collectively, but not individually, pivotal. In auctions, designing for contextual privacy requires choosing an initial question posed to each agent and the order for querying agents. Ascending-join protocols are maximally contextually private for k-item Vickrey auctions. (JEL D44, D82)

5b51167fb0:1a15b1cd2416f9fe.title: Manipulation-Robust Prediction
5b51167fb0:1a15b1cd2416f9fe.author: info@aeaweb.org (Daniel Björkegren1, Joshua E. Blumenstock2 and Samsun Knight3 1 Columbia University (email: dan@bjorkegren.com) 2 UC Berkeley (email: jblumenstock@berkeley.edu) 3 University of…
5b51167fb0:1a15b1cd2416f9fe.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3263-3293 Abstract An increasing number of decisions are guided by machine learning algorithms. But when consequential decisions are encoded in algorithms, individuals may strategically alter their behavior to achieve desired outcomes. This paper develops an empirical approach that adjusts decision algorithms to anticipate manipulation. By explicitly modeling incentives to manipulate, our approach produces decision rules that are stable under manipulation, even when the rules are fully transparent. We stress-test this approach through a large field experiment in Kenya. When implemented, linear strategy-robust decision rules outperform standard linear models such as LASSO. (JEL C45, C93, D12, D91, G51, O12, O16)

5b51167fb0:a1ffa58aef64f33d.title: Risk-Sharing Tests and Covariate Shocks: Drought, Floods, and Pests in Uganda
5b51167fb0:a1ffa58aef64f33d.author: info@aeaweb.org (Ethan Ligon1 1 University of California, Berkeley (email: ligon@berkeley.edu))
5b51167fb0:a1ffa58aef64f33d.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3294-3329 Abstract Efficient risk sharing implies a simple factor structure for marginal utilities of expenditure (MUEs): Pareto weights divided by a common price. The standard approach infers MUEs from total expenditures, implicitly assuming homothetic preferences, unitary income elasticities, and identical price elasticities. Risk-sharing tests using total expenditures work for idiosyncratic shocks (budgets change, but not prices), but not “covariate” shocks (prices change). I describe all preferences that permit one to infer MUEs from expenditures and estimate nonhomothetic MUEs to test whether covariate shocks are shared efficiently in Uganda. This delivers sensible results; the standard approach suggests that droughts, floods, and pests are beneficial. (JEL D12, D81, O12, O13, Q12)

5b51167fb0:797852c7470100e9.title: Optimal Public Transportation Networks: Evidence from the World's Largest Bus Rapid Transit System in Jakarta
5b51167fb0:797852c7470100e9.author: info@aeaweb.org (Gabriel Kreindler1, Arya Gaduh2, Tilman Graff3, Rema Hanna4 and Benjamin A. Olken5 1 Harvard University (email: gkreindler@g.harvard.edu) 2 University of Arkansas (email:…
5b51167fb0:797852c7470100e9.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3330-3379 Abstract Designing public transport networks involves trade-offs between coverage, service frequency, and direct service. We use the expansion of the bus system in Jakarta, Indonesia, to study these trade-offs. We analyze how new direct connections, changes in bus travel time, and wait-time reductions affect bus ridership and aggregate flows and estimate a transit network demand model by matching the route launch events. Commuters in Jakarta are 2–3 times more sensitive to wait time than bus time and inattentive to long routes. We develop a flexible framework to characterize optimal networks. A less concentrated network would increase ridership and commuter welfare. (JEL L92, L98, O18, R41, R42, R48)

5b51167fb0:07fc24e40491cd16.title: Corporate Tax Cuts, Firm Growth, and Workers' Earnings
5b51167fb0:07fc24e40491cd16.author: info@aeaweb.org (Patrick J. Kennedy1, Christine L. Dobridge2, Paul Landefeld3 and Jacob Mortenson4 1 UCLA, NBER, and JCT (email: pkennedy@econ.ucla.edu) 2 Federal Reserve Board (email:…
5b51167fb0:07fc24e40491cd16.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3380-3422 Abstract We study the effects of the largest corporate income tax cut in US history on firms and workers. To identify causal effects, we use employer-employee matched tax records and event studies comparing similarly sized firms in the same industry that faced divergent tax changes due to their preexisting legal status. Tax cuts cause increases in firms' investment, sales, profits, employment, and payrolls, with earnings gains concentrated among highly paid workers. In the short run, 87 percent of private income gains flow to the top 10 percent of the income distribution. (JEL D22, D31, G31, H25, H32, J23, L25)

5b51167fb0:3ee043839f43fb4e.title: Marriage, Fertility, and Cultural Integration in Italy
5b51167fb0:3ee043839f43fb4e.author: info@aeaweb.org (Alberto Bisin1 and Giulia Tura2 1 New York University (email: alberto.bisin@nyu.edu) 2 LUISS University (email: gtura@luiss.it))
5b51167fb0:3ee043839f43fb4e.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3423-3463 Abstract We study cultural integration as an equilibrium outcome of marital matching along cultural and education lines and intrahousehold investment decisions regarding fertility and cultural socialization. Our model allows us to identify cultural-ethnic-group-specific investment parameters and spousal preferences for marital matching. Structural estimates reveal a strong demand to preserve cultural identity on the part of immigrants and limited acceptance of the immigrants' cultural diversity on the part of natives. Furthermore, these estimates reveal a substantial heterogeneity of the parental value of children's education across cultures. Nonetheless, our estimates simulate substantial—though heterogeneous—cultural integration rates across immigrant groups. (JEL D13, J12, J13, J15, Z13)

5b51167fb0:26e7d435f0796a13.title: Defying Distance? The Provision of Medical Services in the Digital Age
5b51167fb0:26e7d435f0796a13.author: info@aeaweb.org (Amanda Dahlstrand1 1 University of Zurich (email: amanda.dahlstrand@econ.uzh.ch))
5b51167fb0:26e7d435f0796a13.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3464-3509 Abstract Digital platforms reduce geographic frictions, enabling better matching between service providers and users. I quantify reallocation gains in Swedish online health care, using nationwide time-conditional random assignment between patients and physicians. Matching high-risk patients with doctors effective at reducing Emergency Room visits lowers such visits by 4.4 percent (SE 1.3); reallocations also reduce Counter-Guideline antibiotics by 3.1 percent (1.4). I find limited trade-offs in matching; horizontal differentiation among doctors and varied patient needs allow improvement in multiple outcomes simultaneously. Efficiency-enhancing reallocations also affect equity. The findings highlight the potential for care reorganization aligning provider heterogeneity with patient needs when geographic constraints are lifted. (JEL C78, H51, I11, I13, I14, I18)

5b51167fb0:221f12c25326ebda.title: The Environmental Bias of Corporate Income Taxation
5b51167fb0:221f12c25326ebda.author: info@aeaweb.org (Luigi Iovino1, Thorsten Martin2 and Julien Sauvagnat3 1 Bocconi University (email: luigi.iovino@unibocconi.it) 2 Frankfurt School of Finance and Management (email: t.martin@fs.de) 3…
5b51167fb0:221f12c25326ebda.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3510-3551 Abstract We study the relationship between corporate income taxation and carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions in the United States. We show CO2-intensive firms benefit more from the tax advantage of debt and pay lower income taxes on their capital income. Building on these new facts, we provide evidence that a cut in the corporate income tax rate leads to a larger expansion of clean firms. We develop a multisector general equilibrium model that accounts for our evidence and quantify the impact of corporate tax reforms on aggregate emissions. A policy that eliminates the tax advantage of debt could reduce aggregate emissions without affecting GDP. (JEL D22, G32, H25, H32, Q52, Q54, Q58)

5b51167fb0:273a7079633c9788.title: Rationing by Race
5b51167fb0:273a7079633c9788.author: info@aeaweb.org (Manasvini Singh1 and Atheendar Venkataramani2 1 Carnegie Mellon University and NBER (email: msingh01@cmu.edu) 2 University of Pennsylvania and NBER (email:…
5b51167fb0:273a7079633c9788.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3552-3585 Abstract We document how deepening resource scarcity results in rationing on the basis of race in a high-stakes setting: health care. Using detailed, time stamped data on 107,000 inpatient admissions to a large health system, we find that in-hospital mortality increases for Black but not White patients as hospitals reach capacity. These findings are not explained by differential patient selection. We identify rationing by wait times as a mechanism, documenting that sicker Black patients wait longer for care than healthier White patients at almost all capacity levels. Text analysis of unstructured clinical notes reveals rationing of provider effort as another mechanism. (JEL I11, I12, I14, J15)

5b51167fb0:b142b734d632b9cc.title: Intergenerational Impacts of Secondary Education: Experimental Evidence from Ghana
5b51167fb0:b142b734d632b9cc.author: info@aeaweb.org (Esther Duflo1, Pascaline Dupas2, Elizabeth Spelke3 and Mark Walsh4 1 MIT and Collège de France (email: eduflo@mit.edu) 2 Princeton University (email: pdupas@princeton.edu) 3 Harvard…
5b51167fb0:b142b734d632b9cc.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3586-3621 Abstract We provide experimental evidence on the intergenerational impacts of secondary education subsidies in a low-income context, leveraging a randomized controlled trial and 15-year longitudinal follow-up. Secondary school scholarships delay fertility, reduce unwanted pregnancies, and change partner selection. Under-one mortality is reduced by half. We also document cognitive development gains of 0.24 standard deviations of test scores by age five among children of female scholarship recipients. Means-tested secondary school scholarships are a high-return investment, with a conservatively estimated US$4.1 in benefits for each US$1 the policy would cost the government in the long run. (JEL H52, I12, I21, I26, J13, J16, O15)

21113a7a19:603639c33f400b49.summary: The not-so-secret secret of building a good school is to have good students. And sometimes that can lead to conflicts between the desire to build better school systems to serve children in the aggregate, and the desire to put your child in the best school for him or her. A NYT columnist talks about this, writing "In New York, a combination of housing segregation and “academic” sorting, called school choice , that begins as early as pre-K means most Black students — even middle-class ones — are forced to attend racially segregated schools with high rates of poverty." (emphasis added) In Fighting for Every Black Child, Did I Betray My Own? A decade ago, I made a decision about my daughter’s education that I hoped would challenge New York City’s separate and unequal school system. Now 16, she thinks I made the wrong choice. By Nikole Hannah-Jones ####### On a somewhat related note, when I speak to prospective PhD students who are visiting universities after being admitted to multiple PhD programs, I encourage them to talk to the graduate students already there, and discover how happy, productive, and collaborative they are. A good PhD program is one where you learn a lot by collaborating with your fellow students in study and research.
